t: This is the home of the Galton Laboratory, part of University College London. It was founded by Francis Galton, the Victorian polymath who originated eugenics and helped lay the foundations of behavioural genetics. It began as the Galton Laboratory of National Eugenics. Over time its work moved to biometry and statistics, and eventually human genetics. Early researchers such as Karl Pearson were inspired by Galton's quantitative approach. The laboratory kept its name until 2020, so what you're standing by is a piece of the history of heredity science, including its troubling beginnings.
